title: whiB7, eis, and injectable RNA
dek: WhiB7 is a transcriptional feeder for eis and other resistance-ish genes. eis promoter-up is kanamycin’s common low-level trick. Do not equate it with rrs 1401 amikacin resistance.
story: eis encodes an acetyltransferase that inactivates kanamycin more readily than amikacin. Promoter-up mutations (and some whiB7 mutations that increase eis expression) yield low-level KAN-R with variable AMK effect — often still AMK-S. rrs a1401g is the high-level cross-R injectable allele.

WhiB7 is a redox-sensitive transcription factor that feeds eis, tap, and other genes. Rare whiB7 mutants can look like an eis-promoter phenocopy. Catalogue rows here have moved between editions; version-stamp them.
Clinically, kanamycin is retired from preferred regimens. This plate exists so a BAM does not scare a programme off amikacin salvage — or, conversely, so rrs 1401 is not ignored because eis is WT.
deep: tlyA loss: capreomycin (and some viomycin) resistance. Not eis.
rrs 1401: AMK, KM, and often CAP. That is the bad rrs.
Do not stack KM+AMK. History already lost that fight.
whiB7 also touches intrinsic macrolide-ish stories that are not TB therapy.
